Payments needed 23 files outside its own code (service-footprint.sh payments, previous lesson); payments.yaml is its manifest in the config repository's base.

The loop copies every .yaml file of templates/dotnet-service/ into a temporary folder, replacing __SERVICE__ with the name and __DIGEST__/__MIGRATE_DIGEST__ with the given digests; the comment says later template changes do not reach the files.

The script runs the checks the config repository gets in CI: kubectl kustomize builds the folder, then kubeconform, from the image pinned as KUBECONFORM in ci.yml, validates every object against Kubernetes 1.34.

claims.text: golden-path.md steps: code with a Dockerfile building service and migration images like DonHang.Payments/Dockerfile; run new-service.sh; copy files to config repo with real digests, open a PR; not-self-service steps one PR each; SLO in docs/design/slo.md before real traffic.

Path gives: probes /health/live and /health/ready, security context like api's, a Service, migration as an Argo CD hook before the Deployment, NetworkPolicies denying ingress and allowing egress only to PostgreSQL (DNS from the namespace's dns-egress policy), images by digest, CI-passing files.

The team keeps: code and tests; migrations and keeping the database working with the previous version; its SLO and what to do when the error budget runs out; CPU and memory requests, which the template sets small to start.

A team with a reason (e.g. a service not built on .NET, another way to deploy) may leave the path, records it in the PR with the reason, and then writes and checks its own manifests (the doc adds keeping up with template changes and answering review questions).

Files rendered once do not follow later template changes, so a rule every service must keep is held by a check on every manifest (require-image-digest in the cluster, kubeconform in CI), not by the template alone.

claims.text: Files written off the path meet the same CI checks once they sit in a folder CI's manifests job checks (kubectl kustomize, kubeconform); kubeconform checks each object against the Kubernetes API schemas and with -strict fails on an unknown field.
claims.source_hint: .github/workflows/ci.yml job manifests; docs/team/platform-capabilities.md row 'Job CI manifests' at stage-4; kubeconform README (-strict)

claims.text: A golden path is a default, not a rule: the template makes it easy to be right at the start, checks catch mistakes later whatever produced the file; the path gives what every service shares, while code, migrations and SLO stay the team's.

Trade-offs: copying meets only the copied service's rules; the golden path meets rules at the start and holds them by checks; a mandatory template blocks unusual services; checks only find rules one failure at a time. The path fits when most services share one shape.

claims.text: Choices: a service not built on .NET → leave the path with the reason recorded, the team keeps its manifests, checks still apply; a changed template default → add a check if it must hold everywhere, else tell teams; a switch per difference → keep the template to what most services share.

claims.text: Each template option is a decision every team must make and a combination the checks must cover, so a template full of options stops being a default.
